summary: Boise NF fire-detection site since 1921; log cab 1922, current L-4 cab 1954 or 1958; no longer staffed, platform closed to visitors.

facts.status_note: Standing, but kept only for emergency duty and not staffed (NHLR); the Forest Service page lists the site as closed.

access.note: Forest Service page lists the site as closed and says no access is allowed to the observation platform. Summit is reached by a gated 4WD road, open June 15 to September 15 per the climbing guide.

visit.trail_note: 4WD road to the summit (FSR-251 via FS-327), gated but open June 15 to September 15 per the climbing guide. Platform closed; check with the Idaho City Ranger District first.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Boise National Forest

events.note: Eula G. Morton appointed fire lookout, April 1921, per a clipping reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page. NHLR dates the peak's use as a fire detection site to 1921.
First structure: a log cabin built on the ground. Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Forest Lookouts page give the same year.
W. F. Cable lived alone at the lookout through the spring and summer. Clipping dated January 3, 1926, so the season is inferred as 1925.
William Rafferty went to the lookout in June 1929; the trip took two days by pack horse.
Eula Bibo, who first worked the station in 1921, returned for the summer. Her son John, 16, worked in her place on Sundays.
Current cab (Region 1 Plan / L-4) replaced the 1922 ground cabin on a 10-foot concrete base. Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com give different years; see resolved_conflicts.
Idaho Fire Lookouts dates its L-4 cab on an 8-foot concrete base to 1958.
Registered September 27, 2020 as NHLR US 1428, ID 120.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and the Forest Lookouts page give 1954; firelookout.com gives 1954 with a question mark; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 1958. The story reports the register's 1954 and notes the disagreement.
NHLR and the Forest Lookouts page describe a 10-foot concrete base; Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com describe 8 feet.

NHLR says kept for emergency duty and Idaho Fire Lookouts says drive-up emergency status; the climbing guide says it is no longer in use; the Forest Service says the site is closed and the platform is not open. The story treats it as unstaffed with the platform closed.
NHLR gives 8,733 ft; firelookout.com gives 8731 ft; a 1945 clipping gives 8752 feet. The brief's 2661.8 m is consistent with NHLR's 2,662 m.

notes_for_editor: Build year of current cab disputed (1954 vs 1958). Date staffing ended not found in sources. Brief's kind 'ground' fits the 1922 cabin; the current cab sits on a concrete base and the Forest Lookouts page calls it two-story, so consider kind two_story. No fire at this lookout was found. No rental found. The 1958 'Swan Home' clipping on the Forest Lookouts page is a different place and was not used. The FS page says 'Last updated September 21, 2026' and carries a header notice 'UPDATED Sept. 19 - Crooked Fire Area, Road, and Trail Closure'; the notice does not name this site, so the reason for the site closure is not confirmed. The Forest Lookouts page is the only source with clippings for the 1920s to 1940s staffing.
